_about.purpose: 20 paired English/Arabic questions for exercising the APP end to end, not the retriever in isolation. Covers the four things the app does that eval_set_v2.json does not touch: spelling repair, follow-up rewriting, continuation replay, and the Arabic round trip.
_about.arabic: Hand-written in Egyptian-flavoured Arabic, NOT produced by translating the English through qwen3. eval_set_ar.json is machine-translated by the same model that then translates it back for retrieval, which flatters itself - the model reliably undoes its own word choices. These do not have that round trip, so an Arabic miss here is a real miss. They are still not user-collected: mark review=human only after a native speaker has read them.
_about.gold: Every answerable question is taken from eval_set_v2.json with its verified doc and must_include, except APP-17 which was added from MHR08 §2.1/§4.1.12 while debugging the accommodation query.
_about.scoring: must_include entries that are form codes or figures are checked in BOTH languages - they survive translation. Prose entries are checked in English only, because an Arabic answer fails English substring matching for reasons that have nothing to do with the pipeline. See eval_app.py.

questions.probes: spelling repair - this is the query that exposed the typo bug
questions.question_en: How far should employees live to get access to accommodation?
questions.question_en_typo: how far should employees live to get access to accomdation
questions.question_ar: الموظف لازم يسكن على بعد كام كيلومتر عن مقر العمل عشان ياخد سكن من الشركة؟
questions.expected_answer: More than 160 km round trip between residence and project area (§4.1.12).
questions.note: NEEDS top_k>=8, and the reason is worth reading before treating a refusal here as a bug. Two different chunks carry '160'. §2.1 ranks 2nd and is a DEFINITION - it says who the policy applies to ('an expatriate whose place of residence ... is 160 kilometers away from the workplace'), not what earns you housing. §4.1.12 is the actual eligibility RULE - 'allowed to accommodate ... if the distance ... exceeds 160 kilometers round trip' - and it ranks 7th, because it shares no wording with the question ('far', 'live', 'access' appear nowhere in it). At top_k<=6 the model sees only the definition and answers 'Not specified', which is defensible. At top_k=8 it answers correctly and says 'more than 160 kilometres'. Measured: refuses at 3, 5 and 6; answers at 8. Also note the source document is internally inconsistent - §2.1's 160 km reads one-way, §4.1.12's is round trip, a factor of two.
questions.brittleness: With identical retrieved chunks and temperature=0/seed=0, 'how far ... accommodation' answers from the §2.1 definition while 'How far ... accommodation' refuses. A capital letter flips it. That is the model sitting on the fence over whether a definition answers the question - the instability is the signal, not the capital.
